registering_session: S70, pre-score, CPU documentation and provenance only
purpose: Record, before any S69 calibration or test score, that the registered difficulty weight w = p(1-p) was inert at batch_pairs = 1, and that it is now realized by a corpus-mean denominator (weight-normalization corpus) with the shuffled order retained as the primary and difficulty-proportional ordering recorded as an implemented sensitivity knob, plus per-step realized-update telemetry. No objective, hyperparameter, budget, selection rule, win bar or scoring rule changes.

amends.rule: the registered file is not edited; this amendment records only the realization of the weight it already registers, the corpus now built for it, and the launch commands
amends_sections: training.objective (realization of the weight only; the functional form is unchanged)
training.batch_pairs (the denominator that made the weight inert)

where: oracle/frontier/preference.py (pre-S70 batch loss divided by the batch weight sum)
defect.mechanism: the batch loss was (sum_i w_i L_i) / (sum_i w_i); at one pair per optimizer step the denominator is that pair's own w_i, so the ratio is L_i and the registered weight cancels exactly
defect.consequence: w(p) = p(1-p) had no effect on the loss, gradient or update in any pre-S70 run, including every S63/S64 preference run; the launcher already drops w <= 0 before budgeting, so no zero-weight pair masked it

scores_existing_at_discovery.what_existed: rollout, pair-construction and frozen-reference-cache receipts only; no calibration or test score

weight_normalization.rule: divide sum_i w_i L_i by the corpus mean weight over the positive-weight pairs, computed once from the filtered pair file and recorded in the arm receipt

pre_s70_comparator.status: retained only to reproduce pre-S70 runs; must not be used for an S69 score

sensitivity_knob.status: implemented and tested; not part of the primary run; not used to select a checkpoint, cadence or arm

pair_order.why_primary_is_shuffled: it reproduces the pre-S70 stream from the seed, so the only realized difference in the primary arm is the denominator

realized_update_telemetry.why: AdamW's per-parameter normalization cancels a constant gradient rescale; a loss value alone does not show that the weight is realized, and a per-step update norm tagged with the pair weight does

unchanged_by_this_amendment: the objective functional form: -log sigmoid(beta * [(s+ - s-) - (r+ - r-)])
mean token-length normalization of sequence log-probabilities
LoRA rank 64, alpha 32, every text-tower linear layer except the output head, base frozen
the identical-effective-problem-set rule for the preference arm and the matched SFT control (drop w <= 0 before budgeting)
the recovery arm's matched mean positive weight
calibration-only selection: highest MATH-cal, tie-break higher GSM8K-cal then earlier cadence
the MMLU-cal retention filter and the adoption gate
the win bar: MATH-500 and full MATH paired 95% intervals above zero; GSM8K and MMLU point delta and interval lower bound not worse than -1.0
the one-shot test scoring rule and the no-enlargement clause
the frozen reference identity (pi_ref is the S67 soup champion)

implementation.measurement_claim: the pre-fix configuration (shuffled, batch) and the primary post-fix configuration (shuffled, corpus) produce different parameter trajectories under torch.optim.AdamW with clip_grad_norm_(1.0), by the test's stated tolerance; the test and its receipt carry the magnitudes, and none is restated in prose
implementation.precision: a constant gradient rescale alone is cancelled by AdamW; the realized difference in the primary arm exists because the sampled pair's weight varies from step to step, so the optimiser moments mix differently-scaled gradients. The weighted order is a second, independent knob and is not active in the primary run.

would_have_been_wrong: re-selecting any threshold, win-bar clause, retention bound, sample limit or cadence
changing the calibration adoption gate or the tie-break rule
reading any test split, or any calibration item, before the correction was committed
adopting or re-selecting the soup coefficient alpha after seeing test results
switching the primary order to weighted, which changes which pair each step sees and is a different experiment
scoring an S69 arm with --weight-normalization batch and calling it the registered objective
rebuilding the corpus with different filters or weights to make the fix look cleaner
presenting the correction as a change to the hypothesis, or as a result

ledger.sha256_source: ledger.sha256 in results/artifacts/stage2/s69-rollouts/soup-receipt.json, re-hashed on disk before this amendment was written

recovery.weight_basis: mean positive p(1-p) of the on-policy problems

frozen_reference_caches.identity: pi_ref is the checkpoint the student is initialised from

statistical_limitation.no_expectation_of_clearing_the_bar: no power calculation justifies an expectation that the win bar is cleared; none is offered
statistical_limitation.null_reporting_rule: a null result is reported as a null result with its interval, its width and the corpus size that produced it; it is not re-framed as underpowered, not rescued by re-scoring a different split, and not replaced by a favourable secondary instrument
statistical_limitation.effective_set_note: the normal arm's effective problem set is the subset with p > 0; the 155 p = 0 problems are the recovery arm's source only, and many p = 1 problems contribute no preference contrast

reference_identity_disclosure.initial_margin: exactly zero, because the student and the reference are the same weights at step zero
consequences: the DPO margin is a displacement from the start point, not a preference between two independently trained policies
the reference term is an anchor to the champion; it bounds drift and cannot distinguish movement toward the chosen side from distance from the champion
the reward difference is not identifiable as an external judge's preference
the chosen side is a verified-correct teacher continuation and the rejected side is the student's own failure, so part of the margin is teacher-versus-student quality
a win is attributable to the pair construction, the objective and the anchor-to-start, not to the choice of an independent reference model

memory_sizing.rule: SELVEDGE_MEM = max(1.5 x peak, peak + 1 GiB), where peak = max(peak_reserved_gib, peak_allocated_gib, cgroup memory_peak in GiB) from the arm's own smoke receipt
memory_sizing.smoke_bound: 20g is a bound, not a measurement
memory_sizing.recorded_in: the launch record and the arm receipt's cgroup_memory block

arms.role: attribution control on the identical effective problem set
the p = 0 teacher pairs at the matched mean positive weight

run_plan.per_arm_directories_reason: the merged checkpoint filenames ckpt-<step>.pt are not arm-tagged, so a shared out-dir could silently overwrite one arm's checkpoint with another's
